title: 2005 AMC 10B Problem 7
statement: A circle is inscribed in a square, then a square is inscribed in this circle, and finally, a circle is inscribed in this square. What is the ratio of the area of the smaller circle to the area of the larger square?

solutions.text:
Let the smaller circle have radius \(r,\) so its area is \(\pi r^2.\)

The smaller square, which circumscribes this circle, has side \(2r,\) and its diagonal \(2\sqrt2\,r\) is the diameter of the larger circle. So the larger circle has radius \(\sqrt2\,r.\)

The larger square circumscribes the larger circle, so it has side \(2\sqrt2\,r\) and area \(8r^2.\)

The desired ratio is \[ \dfrac{\pi r^2}{8r^2} = \dfrac{\pi}{8}. \]

Thus, B is the correct answer.
hints: Let the smaller circle have radius \(r\) and work outward
The larger circle’s radius is half the diagonal of the smaller square, \(\sqrt2\,r\)
